claims.text: Powder-metallurgy incorporation of hBN into CoCrFeNi will produce a uniformly dispersed hBN phase.
Coupling agents and sintering aids can provide strong interfacial bonding between hBN and the CoCrFeNi matrix.
The embedded hBN platelets will remain stable and well bonded throughout thermal cycling from room temperature to 800 °C.
During sliding, hBN at the wear interface will facilitate formation of a lubricious tribolayer.
The hBN-derived tribolayer will continuously replenish during sliding.
The hBN-derived tribolayer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
The thermal stability of hBN will preserve its lubricating effect at temperatures up to 800 °C.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will diminish friction.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact will diminish wear.
The CoCrFeNi–hBN composite will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The CoCrFeNi–hBN composite will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The proposed friction and wear benefits will apply under sliding loads of 10–20 N in ambient air.
Performance across the stated test range is contingent on uniform hBN dispersion and robust interfacial bonding.
Inconsistent powder-metallurgy processing may prevent achievement of the required hBN dispersion and interfacial bonding.
